BOOT HISTORY 2026-11-11 (arm 5, receipts `head:~/benchmarks/arm5-fi073c-20261111/`, recipe `recipes/ds4/zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm5-fi073.yaml`, quartet tp 4; row and claim stay). Boot 1 was engine-impossible target-only: `deepseek_v4_hook.py:108` admits only EAGLE/DSPARK, so `SPEC_ALGO` never reaches it and the launcher's own `RECIPE_ENV` silently clobbers `-o env.SPEC_ALGO=off`; the only working disable is the last `--speculative-algorithm` in `EXTRA_SGLANG_ARGS`, and the engine refused rather than run target-only. Boots 2 and the unmodified arm-3 control died identically in `ncclCommInitRank` (`ibv_modify_qp 61`, empty GID), which is fleet state, not the port. Boot 3, with an explicit `NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX` override, passed `Init parallel` (49.35 s), loaded target (130.41 s) and draft (4.00 s), captured all nine target graphs, and died at t~307 s on the prefill envelope. Boot 4, after the 06:33-06:38Z full parallel fleet reboot (kernel 7.0.0-1024 -> 1025) restored contiguous GID tables, passed NCCL on sparkrun's own injected env and died on the same stopper. Canary NOT measured. STOPPER: `ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=193 ... (num_tokens <= 64)` from `_forward_trtllm_prefill` -- the port drives the decode kernel one table row per token and FlashInfer's decode instantiation caps at 64. Chunking cannot fix it: `chunked_prefill_size % page_size == 0` with page size forced to 256, and disabling chunking is refused by the trtllm backend. Root cause of boots 2-3: a fleet-wide carrier flap at 2026-11-11T02:44:36Z left plane A's GID index 3 vacated while plane B stayed contiguous; sparkrun injects one `NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX` derived from the first active HCA and applies it to both rails (`scripts/ib_detect.sh:44-45`, `infiniband.py:246,268`), so index 3 is invalid on plane A. Recorded as `sparkrun-single-gid-index-for-two-hcas`; repair belongs in sparkrun or cluster config, never a recipe env line. Next route is `ds4-arm5-prefill-route-delta8`, which blocks this row.

OWNER 2026-11-11 (#1/#4): this session's first work, and the build half is paid — rebuild the image on the build node, carry it to four ranks, boot the canary. The port is now SIX deltas: the sixth is the DSpark draft path, which hands the ported decode call an FP8 query and trips the port's own BF16 assert (latest boot 2026-11-11T01:50:58Z: AssertionError: SM12x sparse MLA needs BF16 query, got torch.float8_e4m3fn at deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py:361 via dspark_worker_v2.py:515 init_cuda_graphs -> deepseek_v4_dspark.py:760), and patch_dsv41_fi073.py still writes only models/deepseek_v4.py, touching nothing in models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py. The 96-row envelope is already bypassed: that same boot ran with CUDA_GRAPH_MAX_BS_DECODE=10 and captured bs 10..4 before the assert, so the row-limit error is no longer the stopper. Made machine-runnable on the arm that actually measures — recipe recipes/ds4/zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm5-fi073.yaml, quartet, tp 4. The three machine-runnable fields were silently dropped once by a stale-snapshot write in the fold that recorded this round; re-applied through `update` and verified in `queue --json` 2026-11-11. Provenance: mad-science/TODO.md §"Settled questions" ## Owner round 2026-11-11 — TP>=4 survey S1/S4; .scratch/tp4-survey/evidence.md §1. Claimed 2026-11-11 as this session's in-flight work (`session:tp4-20261111`) — a director session, not a campaign lease, so no campaign may lease and boot this arm before the sixth delta lands under `ds4-arm5-dspark-bf16-query-delta`. | PORT PLAN (design note: mad-science/SM121-SPARSE-MLA-PORT.md, section 'Port A'). Not blocked on hardware: FlashInfer ships the SM121 kernel, the fork calls a different one. Three deltas, all verified against image `:0.2.1` (sha256:85c1ffc3...): (1) deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py:366,506 hardcode backend="trtllm-gen", which is SM100/103-only in every release through v0.7.4rc2 (flashinfer/mla/_core.py:1241-1244; :1062 at v0.6.18 is the recorded error verbatim); SM12x has its own backend, is_sm120_family = cc in ((12,0),(12,1)) -> "auto" resolves "sparse" (_core.py:1226-1255, since v0.7.0). (2) the fork passes the pre-0.7 single sparse_indices / sparse_topk_lens pair; 0.7.x SM12x splits the pools (swa_kv_cache + swa_topk_lens, compressed via extra_sparse_indices / extra_sparse_topk_lens) with kv_cache_format naming the storage form - both call sites (:354, :493) need re-plumbing, not a rename. (3) the monkeypatch target _fi_core._get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer (:102) is gone in 0.7.3; both call sites already pass multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer= (a 0.7.3 kwarg), so guard the install path instead of letting it raise AttributeError at first decode. IMAGE GATE: needs one image with BOTH the knapcio adapter (/opt/dsv41/boot.py + adapter sitecustomize + b12x) AND FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 with the sm121a provider; none exists locally - :0.2.1, canary-roce-aff52fa5, canary-roce-20261022, c3-reconciled:103ad321 are all 0.6.18, and the only 0.7.3 image (nightly-dev-cu13-20261110-4a5c6b8f) has no /opt/dsv41. BUILD SHAPE: rebuild :0.2.1's Dockerfile (base ~/builds/deepgemm-sm121/ctx/Dockerfile.sm121) with FlashInfer 0.7.3 + flashinfer_jit_cache_sm121a 0.7.3; .35 is free for builds (2026-11-10). pip overlay exists (79.8 MB python wheel sha256 548a3ea1..., 234 MB sm121a provider sha256 e5059124...b01ed) but fixes none of (2)-(3) - do not prefer it. node_cost is the build host; ACCEPTANCE needs a quartet: (a) flashinfer.__version__ == 0.7.3 in-image, (b) --dsv4-attn-backend trtllm admitted (hook gate already widened at deepseek_v4_hook.py:58), (c) first decode step clean and the log names the sparse backend, (d) C1/C2 cell same-window vs arm-3-control (:0.2.1, replay off). FALSIFIER for the silent-wrong-logits class: not a throughput cell - send the shipped production canary's own prompt (same checkpoint, same hardware, flashmla route) and compare the greedy answer TEXT; a backend that skipped the compressed segment or mis-ordered SWA indices still passes every gate and only this comparison catches it. estimate: provisional.

No flag can work: --dsa-* is resolved first, then Ernie5_5MlaAttnBackend.__init__ assigns over it after super().__init__() - self.dsa_prefill_impl = self.dsa_decode_impl = "flashmla_sparse" (ernie55_backend.py:83-85) - so flashinfer_sparse_mla is rejected by the parent GLM-only whitelist (flash_mla_sm120.py:678-713) before the pin and every other value is discarded after it. config.json has no learnable_sink; the sink is add_full_attention_sink_bias + learnable_sink_param. No machine shape can express six nodes yet (tp is 1/2/4), so this row stays non-machine-runnable (no recipe/tp): the claim is the campaign's own lease (S9b), which lands as campaign-six-node-claim and is also what blocks it structurally. Provenance: mad-science/TODO.md §"Settled questions" ## Owner round 2026-11-11 — TP>=4 survey S3/S9; .scratch/tp4-survey/evidence.md §6. | SIX-NODE SHAPE as TP=2 x PP=3, registered as a RESEARCH row (no `recipe`/`tp` fields, node_cost blank) because the tool requires `tp` to equal a `node_cost` from (single/pair/quartet) and there is no six-node value, and because a full-fleet window must never be leased by the campaign — it is a declared window (precedent: mistral-large-4-1t-feasibility, whose node_cost is blank on purpose). The arm's recipe is `recipes/explore/kimi-k3.1-pro-pruned75-mxfp4-vllm-tp4.yaml`, launched with tp 2 and pipeline_parallel 3 over all six nodes. The only term of the right size for Kimi is the rank count: 442.833 GiB / 6 = 73.80 GiB/rank, heads 96/2 = 48 (ok), routed intermediate 3584/2 = 1792 (ok), dense 33792/2 (ok), vocab 163840/2 (ok), and each rank takes 1/3 of the 93 layers; `sparkrun/runtimes/vllm_distributed.py:62,264` computes `replica_size = tp*pp`, and real PP evidence, checked not remembered: `recipes/qwen4/qwen3.8-flash-next-nvfp4-solo-vllm-b12x.yaml:61-62` passes `--pipeline-parallel-size {pipeline_parallel}` and `recipes/MECHANICS.md:653-656` states the rule (TP within a node plus `pipeline_parallel_size` = nodes), while the rank arithmetic comes from the INSTALLED package, `sparkrun/src/sparkrun/runtimes/vllm_distributed.py:62,264` (`max(1, p.tensor_parallel * p.pipeline_parallel)`). Predicted floor >=30 GiB. FALSIFIED if the wrapper or the KDA path rejects PP, or a rank reports `weights memory` far above 73.6 GiB. Neither is evidence of infeasibility; both are gates the shape must clear first. | PROVENANCE PATHS ARE CHECKED, NOT REMEMBERED (same pass that caught the 0-shot/8-shot gate): this row's provenance once cited `recipes/qwen4/arms/eugr-qwen3.8-flash-next-nvfp4-cluster.yaml`, which has never existed — `recipes/qwen4/` is flat and no `*cluster*` recipe exists in the tree; the only other hit is `attic/qwen4/ARMS-MANIFEST.md:96`, a frozen contributor inventory that stays as-is. A phantom citation is worse than none: the next session follows it, finds nothing, and concludes the topology is unsupported — the opposite of the question this row asks. tasks.title: DS4 1017 SM121: the 0.77 papered pair — engine coefficient 1,670.75 B/token/rank says both arms hold 1,035,623 tokens one fraction down (replay-on vs replay-off)
tasks.notes: PAPERED PREDICTION, NOT YET RUN — the A/B lane never executed. The engine prints its own coefficient: **1,670.75 B/token/rank** (`DSV4 memory calculation` line, `pool_configurator.py:1553-1568`), and the sizing identity is `full_token = (available_bytes - fixed) / bytes_per_full_token` (`:1531`), which reproduces all four recorded boots to <=0.7 % — so the arithmetic is the engine's, not ours. Only four layers own KV (`kv_source_layer_ids [2,8,14,20]`, `compress_ratios` 2,2,2,1), so 1M costs just 1.66 GiB. Two sensitivities per fraction: `available_bytes` moves +81.7 GiB/fraction replay-off and +67.3 GiB/fraction replay-on, while the host floor moves -17 GiB/fraction. Predicted at 0.77: off `full_token` ~2.29 M with floor ~5.80 GiB, on ~1.57 M with floor >=6.5 GiB — i.e. BOTH arms hold a 1,035,623-token prompt one fraction lower than the shipped 0.78/0.75 attempts, which is the whole point: the pair is the papered prediction the lane has been missing. Arm A = replay-on `recipes/ds4/zz-ds4-1017-sm121-indexer-scoring.yaml`, arm B = replay-off `recipes/ds4/zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm3-control.yaml`, both at `MEM_FRACTION_STATIC=0.77`. GUARD EXPERIMENT ONLY: 5.7 GiB (0.83 GiB above earlyoom's 4.87 line), scoped to this cell and recorded as such, back to 6.0 afterwards; stop rank reads below 5.4 GiB. FALSIFIERS: replay-on `full_token` 1,035,623, or replay-off floor <5.4 GiB during the cell. | MEASURED 2026-11-10 — THE PAIR EXISTS. At 0.77 both arms hold the 1,035,623-token prompt: replay-off `full_token` 2,135,552 with floor 7.64 GiB (C5 370.7 s, 5/5 needles, 0 errors); replay-on 1,997,824 with floor 10.87 GiB (1M cell PASS, and that cell returns the lane's steady-state decode, 31.8 ms/step over 37 steps / 64 tokens). The 0.75->0.77 cost is recorded: 438,528 -> 2,135,552 tokens, C5 282.8 s -> 370.7 s, floor 10.67 -> 7.64 GiB. Both stated falsifiers (replay-on full_token 1,035,623; replay-off floor <5.4 GiB) stayed silent.

tasks.title: DS4 1017 SM121: port the V41/V41_FP4 KV layout so fp4 KV is admissible — dtype is not a lever today, and sizing lies about fp4
tasks.notes: CORRECTION TO THE FP8-KV IDEA this lane carried: KV dtype is NOT a lever here. The line is already `kv_dtype: fp8_e4m3`, and `fp8_ds_mla` is not a value this engine knows — zero occurrences in image commit `103ad321`; it is vLLM's packed MLA row, a different engine. Nor would a narrower dtype move the floor: the pool fills every available byte, so halving bytes/token doubles tokens and leaves the memory pressure (and the floor) where it was. `nvfp4` KV is actively UNSAFE: the sizing path has no fp4 term, so it would print the same 1,670.75 B/token while asking kernels for fp4 rows — the engine would over-advertise budget it cannot back. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY UNLOCK FP4 KV is engine work, and it is two sites plus a branch: relax the `is_sm100` gate at `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:197`, port the `V41`/`V41_FP4` layout from `kv_layout.cuh:38`, and add the fp4 branch in `pool_configurator.py:1024-1035`. That buys 2-4x tokens per GiB (a context win), zero floor — so it is a reason to rebuild, not a reason to expect a boot where none fit. Blocked: engine work, no boot can pass before the port exists.

tasks.title: Served-name test must derive its exception from the recipe’s normalising overlay, not a hand-maintained ALLOWED set (third red-main class tonight)
tasks.notes: THIRD RED-MAIN INCIDENT TONIGHT of one class: a new recipe lands and the test that guards it does not know about it. `recipes/ds4/zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm5-fi073.yaml` renders `--served-model-name {model}`, which is CORRECT for its lane because `mods/dsv41-sglang-overlay/launcher.py` normalises the rendered snapshot path back to the repo id, but `tests/test_recipe_placeholder_resolution.py::ServedModelNameNotRebound.ALLOWED` is a hand-maintained set — so the file landed at `ccffee7`, the census at `099933a` counted it, and two tests stayed red until `17553ae` added the entry (main red for ~20 min across three commits). tasks.title: Container `--memory` bounds host anon and pinned staging only: GB10 CUDA/UVM writes past it, so the cap is a runaway guard and never a replacement for earlyoom
tasks.notes: PROBED, NOT ARGUED. In `docker run --memory=8g --memory-swap=8g --gpus all` on the production image, `torch.zeros(16 GiB, device='cuda')` **succeeded** (`memory.current` 409 MiB, `memory.peak` 443 MiB, `oom_kill` 0, `dmem.current`/`dmem.max` empty) while host `used` went 4 -> 21 GiB. Controls prove the limit is real for the two things it does cover: a 16 GiB host `bytearray` under 8 GiB exits 137 `OOMKilled`, and a 6 GiB `pin_memory` staging buffer under 4 GiB is killed with `peak` exactly 4 GiB. So on GB10 the CUDA/UVM allocations live OUTSIDE the container cgroup, and `--memory` cannot replace earlyoom or the 6.0 GiB host sampler. Field data agrees: the marlin boot dove host to 110.3 GiB with the rank cgroup at <=5.87 GB, and arm5's 128K C5 floored host at 5.54 GiB with cgroup 12.65. SCHEMA: the key exists and is not inert — `executor_config.memory_limit` -> `docker run --memory=` (`core/recipe.py:112`, `orchestration/executor.py:297-304`, `executors/docker.py:457-458`), also reachable as `--memory-limit`/`-o memory_limit=`; `defaults: memory_limit` IS INERT. Documented at `recipes/MECHANICS.md:252-271`. RULE: 2 x measured peak cgroup, ceil to 8 GiB, floor 16 -> 72G for the ds4 quartet arms, 32G for arm5's 128K shape, 16G for marlin, pool ceiling 112G; **none of those fires in any measured failure**, which is the point — the cap is a runaway guard, not a sizing lever. REMAINS: upstream `../sparkrun` `executors/docker.py:457-458` emits no `--memory-swap`, so a breach swaps up to the limit before killing (measured: `memory.swap.max = memory.max`, and `.35` carries 16 GiB swap) — a named one-line unlock, not applied.

tasks.title: A readiness-timeout boot leaks four containers for 32 minutes: the driver never stops the task it launched, and a fabric cut during NCCL init freezes the boot instead of failing it
tasks.notes: The TP=4 driver exits on its own readiness ceiling but **never stops the task it launched**. Measured 2026-11-10: the ERNIE gate boot launched 21:10:28Z, the head lost reachability at ~21:12 (during TP0 Init parallel), the engine came up 21:12:46, `Load weight begin. avail mem=108.78 GB` at 21:13:54, then the last line ever written at 21:13:57 — `multimem all-gather disabled because the TP group spans across nodes` — because the TP weight broadcast could not complete without the fabric. The driver gave up at 1364 s with `endpoint did not become ready — rank-0 readiness probe failed: Timeout`; `/health` and `/v1/models` both `000`; **the four containers then sat up for 32 minutes** (4 GiB baseline each, no weights resident) until a human read the id out of `launch.log` and ran `sparkrun stop sparkrun_e59088ba4d0f3858_9533d15053fe` at 21:43:33Z. TWO MECHANISMS, two different fixes: (1) THE READINESS TIMEOUT DOES NOT TEAR DOWN — a failed boot can leak a serve indefinitely if nobody looks, and the fleet then reads 'busy' to every other session while measuring nothing. Fix: on readiness timeout, `sparkrun stop <own task id>` before exiting, and print the id it used. ACCEPTANCE: a deliberately unfittable boot (or a stubbed endpoint) ends with `ctns=0` on its ranks and the id in the log. (2) A LINK/FABRIC CUT DURING NCCL INIT FREEZES THE BOOT RATHER THAN FAILING IT — the engine wrote its last line 3 s after `Load weight begin` and then nothing for 30 minutes: no crash, no timeout, no error, the weight broadcast simply never completed. So 'still loading' must never be read as healthy past the point where a successful boot would have spoken: the watchdog has to distinguish 'slow' from 'frozen', and a boot whose log stops growing while its endpoint never opens is frozen, not loading — the same `--stall` distinction `tools/boot-watchdog.py` already makes for the healthy case. RELATED, already recorded: arm the watchdog BEFORE the launch, not after the id poll — the bare id is recoverable from `launch.log`, so nothing about arming requires the driver's `NO_TASK_ID` window. | OWNERSHIP, so nobody fixes the same teardown twice: this row owns the sparkrun DRIVER's `sparkrun stop <own task id>` on readiness timeout and the frozen-vs-slow distinction at the driver's endpoint probe; `run-arm-appearance-window-300s` owns the shell-side trap that stops `$TID` and kills `$WD` but never `$LAUNCH`; `run-arm-stall-verdict-reads-as-death` owns the verdict TEXT that merges stall into death; `mem-guard-outlives-its-task` owns guard lifetime. None of those three covers a driver that exits cleanly and leaves four containers up for half an hour. tasks.title: ARM_EXTRA_CLIENT output is not in the campaign measured set: a hook can score 190/200 and still file as no-artefact, so the executor must write the measured shape
tasks.notes: `ARM_EXTRA_CLIENT` CAN RUN AND STILL PRODUCE NOTHING THE DIRECTOR COUNTS. Measured 2026-11-10 while trying to wire the ERNIE gate: the executor reads the hook (`run-arm.sh:879-889`, `ARM_EXTRA_TIMEOUT` default 1800, `timeout -k 30`, output to `extra-client.log`) and the campaign forwards the row's `env` all the way into it (`plan.py:260-262`, `director.py:227-236`, `worker.py:55-56`), but a hook that writes `run_benchmarks.py`'s `<outdir>/<stem>.json` + `_raw/*.jsonl` satisfies NOTHING in `evidence.py:37` (`MEASURED_ARTEFACTS = ladder.json, ladder.transcribed.json, house.json, house.transcribed.txt`), and `run-arm.sh:892` only APPENDS to a `house.yaml` that already exists — deliberately, so an absent marker means 'unfinished'. So a perfect 190/200 client run files as 'no machine-readable artefact' and the director retries: the rc=4 loop, now with a five-minute quality client inside it. FIX, either shape: (a) let the hook write the measured shape — a `house.yaml` carrying `suite`/`ladder` plus the score, or a `house.json`/`ladder.json` the client itself emits; or (b) teach `evidence.py` that a client-shaped result is evidence, keyed on the same field the client writes, and make the marker say which producer it came from. Prefer (a): the marker is the contract every other reader already understands. ACCEPTANCE: an arm whose ONLY artefact is the extra client's output ends `measured` with the artefact path named in the receipt, and a hook that exits nonzero without writing its artefact still ends failed — both covered by tests. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-10, shape (1) — the RUNNER normalises, not the client (`3620460` + `02b7021`; gate run 42929982064). A successful `ARM_EXTRA_CLIENT` now makes `tools/run-arm.sh` write ONE fixed `quality.json` in the receipt root carrying `producer` (component/command/rc/source/files) plus a `client` map of each JSON the hook wrote, parsed and keyed by relative path. It never overwrites an existing `quality.json`, and writes nothing on a failed hook or when the hook left no parseable JSON, so the arm stays failed/retried rather than measured-by-accident. `quality.json` joined `MEASURED_ARTEFACTS` in BOTH implementations (`campaign/sparkrun_campaign/evidence.py` and `tools/next-arms.py`), each with its own content check (`quality_problem()` / `quality_failure()`), and the parity test now carries a valid AND a truncated `quality.json` case — presence alone cannot measure, and drift between the two copies fails the suite. MECHANISM AND LIMITATIONS, stated so nobody re-derives them: discovery is BY IDENTITY, not by timestamp (`1b93c4f`): `run-arm.sh` snapshots a `sha256` per candidate `.json` under the receipt root — excluding `_raw` and the skip set — BEFORE the hook, and normalises files that are new or whose hash changed; an unchanged file from a previous boot is excluded, an overwritten resume result is included, `client/` is inside the same walk, and a missing before-baseline writes nothing rather than guessing. The timestamp filter this replaced was itself a defect: the log's final append happens AFTER the client exits, so a client that writes then prints a summary (`run_benchmarks.py`'s exact shape) had its JSON filtered out and no `quality.json` was written at all — the rc=4 loop returning — and the old test passed only because a `printf` and an `echo` can land in one coarse clock tick. Pinned by three tests: `test_a_client_that_prints_after_writing_still_normalises` (fails on the old code), `test_a_pre_existing_unchanged_json_is_not_this_runs_cell`, `test_an_overwritten_json_is_normalised`. The other limitation stands: a bare scalar JSON is not a cell/score. This closes the rc=4 loop for every client-driven arm — BFCL, house, GSM8K alike — which is why it outranks the individual arms it was opened for.

tasks.title: arm5 fi073 never reaches /health: a rank-asymmetric 2-element all-reduce in replicated_split during the autotune dummy forward times out at 600 s
tasks.notes:
RECORDED VERDICT 2026-11-11, not a fix: the 600 s rank-asymmetric TP all-reduce in the autotune dummy forward is not reproducible on the current tree. The fi073c/fi073d quartet boots passed the same autotune stage repeatedly (boots 3, 4, 5, 5b, 7, 8), and arm 5 then measured end to end (canary 4183, ladder boot7/boot8). The failure stays on record as the reason the fi073b boot died; no code change is claimed to have removed it.

The arm5 fi073 canary boot never reached `/health` because of a **rank-asymmetric 2-element TP all-reduce inside the autotune dummy forward**. `NCCL` on rank 0: `Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=2, OpType=ALLREDUCE, NumelIn=2, NumelOut=2, Timeout(ms)=600000) ran 600003 milliseconds before timing out`, then `Fatal Python error: Aborted`. The engine's own stack names the frames: `all_reduce distributed_c10d.py:3245` <- `_build /opt/dsv41/adapter/replicated_split.py:298` <- `forward replicated_split.py:338` <- `_forward_prepare deepseek_v4.py:1842` <- `forward deepseek_v4.py:2396/4398` <- `l2_prefetch.py:635` <- `verify_cap.py:203` <- `_dummy_run base_runner.py:750` <- `run_flashinfer_autotune_forward flashinfer_autotune.py:308` <- `capture_cuda_graphs cuda_graph_setup.py:391`.

Mechanism (SPECULATIVE, the timeout and frames are VERIFIED): a lazy rebuild keyed on local state gives repeated dummy invocations a different iteration per rank, so one rank enters the collective while its peers do not. The tactic cache was ruled out first, and cheaply — the `.../flashinfer/autotune/0.7.3/sm121/c6258882a5fa03fd/` directory was **empty on all four ranks** (no `rank_tp0_pp0_dp0.json` ever existed), and the older `0.6.18` table for this model parses to `{'_metadata','_generation'}` — zero tuned ops, so there was no precedent to inherit. The first canary boot's 28-minute stall hit the same collective but produced no NCCL timeout inside that window; that residual is unmeasured.

Fix, either shape: compute the rebuild decision once and broadcast it **before** the tune loop, or skip the lazy rebuild while the autotune dummy runs. Constraints that must ride in the row: patch through `recipes/ds4/patch_dsv41_fi073.py` (anchored, fail-closed, Dockerfile compile gate), and **the fix must not alter the non-autotune serving path** — that file is on the steady-state path, so a numerics change there would invalidate every number measured tonight.

PY-SPY GOTCHA (same 20-minute tax, recorded so nobody pays it again): sparkrun already grants `SYS_PTRACE` (`runtimes/_util.py:20-41`), so no recipe change is needed; the documented path is `docker exec -u root <container> py-spy dump`, and an exec as the workload user fails on permissions.

The durable answer is a verify route with its own numerics (a route that admits a 96-row verify call and is proven to score the same root ids as decode), not raising the request cap. Canary `4183`; **16/16 concurrent canaries identical at 96-row target-verify batches** (decode batch `#running-req: 11`, `cuda graph: False`), 0 errors. tasks.title: A board published without one of the In-flight state rows passes every guard, because publish compares bytes and never the row set
tasks.notes: Measured 2026-11-11 03:17-03:25 ET. The 03:14 board (blob 2249062c) carried a `| queue |` row; the 03:17 board (commit `8e160b2`, blob 0f54622c) carried none, and a tick that composes on it and keeps the In flight body verbatim inherits the gap: commit `bc2cc38` published 0 queue rows and passed `publish` (rc=0), `lint` (ok) and the push gate. `9ae7cd4` restored the row and attributed its loss to the composing tick, but the base it composed from already lacked it. This is `board-publish-accepts-weaker-replacement` at row granularity: the guards compare bytes against a base, so a base that is itself missing a state row is indistinguishable from a good one, and no check asserts that the composed In flight carries the expected row keys (census, pool, .30-.35, quartet, queue, window, campaign, publication). Acceptance: publish (or lint) refuses a board whose In flight lacks any expected row key, or whose row set is a strict subset of the base it replaced, with a test carrying both a pass-through and a negative control that drops one row; a peer tick that publishes a shrunken base is caught by the next tick rather than by a human reading the table.

tasks.title: Runtime cache: a root-owned flashinfer subtree breaks rank 3 with PermissionError
tasks.notes: MEASURED 2026-11-11: rank 3's serve died on `PermissionError` for `/cache/runtime/flashinfer/.cache/...`; the host runtime-cache `flashinfer` subtree on `.35` was `0:0` (created 2026-11-11 04:04 EST) while `1000:1000` elsewhere. MECHANISM, named 2026-11-11: the ERNIE mod's hook (`recipes/explore/mods/ernie55-flashinfer-sparse-sglang/run.sh`) runs the verifier as root; the verifier imports `flashinfer`, whose 0.7.3 cache root is `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE/.cache/flashinfer` (default `$HOME`, the shared runtime cache), and the mod reowned only `$MOD_LOGDIR`, so the JIT cache was born root-owned (`mad-science/AGENTS.md` §Mods). The `chown -R 1000:1000` that recovered `.35` is the repair, not the fix. FIX LANDED IN THE MOD 2026-11-11, UNPROVEN UNTIL A BOOT: the hook exports `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` and `TMPDIR` to a mod-owned `/cache/runtime/ernie55-flashinfer-sparse-sglang-verify/` before the import, and refuses the launch if the shared tree gains a root-owned entry or is not cache-owned. ACCEPTANCE: a boot whose hook leaves no root-owned child under `/cache/runtime/flashinfer` (and the two general guards: a preflight that repairs the subtrees it mounts, and a mod writing them reowning what it creates). SPARKRUN SURFACE (owner direction 2026-11-11; read from the installed source, version 0.4.3-alpha+g685ad2f on the head): `sparkrun setup fix-permissions` defaults to `~/.cache/huggingface` and takes `--cache-dir` (`sparkrun/scripts/fix_permissions.sh:7,11` picks `{cache_dir}` else `$TARGET_HOME/.cache/huggingface`; `:15` chowns that one path; CLI options at `sparkrun/cli/_setup/_commands.py:1170,1206`). So the default command does NOT repair what the ERNIE rank died on: the runtime cache is `~/.cache/sparkrun/runtime-cache` on the host and needs `--cache-dir`. Verbatim runs on the head, 2026-11-11: `sparkrun setup fix-permissions --cluster WOPR` -> `Fixing file permissions for user 'red' on 6 host(s)...`, `[OK] .30` .. `[OK] .35: fixed permissions on /home/red/.cache/huggingface`, `Results: 6 fixed.`; the same command with `--cache-dir /home/red/.cache/sparkrun/runtime-cache` -> six `[OK]` lines, one per host, for that path and `Results: 6 fixed.` Post-fix probe on `.35` (the node that failed): `red:red` on the runtime cache and its llama-cpp/sglang/vllm dirs, `root-owned-count=0` under `~/.cache/sparkrun/runtime-cache`. Nothing in sparkrun detects a root-owned subtree. ACCEPTANCE (queued until a boot proves it): the window runs both invocations before boot, or the campaign runs them per lease, with their own output in the receipt and a post-fix probe showing the subtree cache-owned. PREVENTION, landed same day (commit `ba42153`): shared `mods/reown-runtime-cache/` reowns `/cache/runtime/flashinfer /cache/runtime/.cache` to the cache owner and fails the launch if the owner is still not the cache owner; both lanes list it after the mod whose root writes it repairs. No bespoke preflight: the host repair is sparkrun's own command, the container repair is the mod. CLOSED 2026-11-11 — half repair, half prevention, both on file. REPAIR, sparkrun's own command: `sparkrun setup fix-permissions --cluster WOPR` fixed `/home/red/.cache/huggingface` on six hosts (`Results: 6 fixed.`) and the same command with `--cache-dir /home/red/.cache/sparkrun/runtime-cache` fixed the runtime cache on six hosts (`Results: 6 fixed.`, 13.6 s) — the path the rank died in; post-fix probe on `.35` is `red:red` on the runtime cache and its llama-cpp/sglang/vllm dirs with `root-owned-count=0`. PREVENTION, the mod: `mods/reown-runtime-cache` is listed by both recipes and resolved in the measured verify-route boot — its log in that boot's leaf (`.../runtime-cache/sglang/deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-10a02831/modlogs/reown-runtime-cache.log`, 16:34:45Z) reads `USER_UID=1000`, `path /cache/runtime/flashinfer: owner 1000:1000 -> 1000:1000`, `skip: /cache/runtime/.cache does not exist`, `Done. 0 path(s) reowned, all checked against 1000:1000`; the boot reached `Ready` in 273 s and the load-bearing path stayed cache-owned. The mod's fail-closed repair path is unit-tested (`tests/test_reown_runtime_cache_mod.py`: stuck repair exits non-zero and names the path). Nothing in sparkrun detects a root-owned subtree, so the mod is the guard.

tasks.title: Use sparkrun logs for per-rank receipts; keep engine-exit-capture for docker-event/OOM attribution
tasks.notes: AUTHORING 2026-11-11, estimate 2 h provisional. `sparkrun logs <recipe|cluster-id> -a` reads `/tmp/sparkrun_serve.log` on the head and on every rank (`sparkrun/core/log_source.py:35`), so a receipt should carry the native per-rank output plus the native command that produced it, instead of a hand-rolled `docker logs`/`ssh cat` capture. `tools/engine-exit-capture.sh` stays only for what no log command can answer: the `--rm` die-event race (the daemon deletes a dead container ~26 ms after the event) and OOM/kernel attribution. ACCEPTANCE: one boot's receipt carries the native command and its per-rank output verbatim. DONE 2026-11-11: `run-arm.sh`'s harvest section runs, before the stop, `sparkrun logs <task-id> -a -H <HOSTS> --cluster WOPR` and splits the CLI's `[host/role] ` prefix into `logs/<host>-serve.log`; `native-logs-command.txt` records the exact command, the binary's `--version` and rc; `native-logs-status.txt` records per-host lines/bytes and names a missing rank (`missing-rank <host> bytes=0`) instead of skipping it; the raw stream and stderr stay in `native-logs.raw`/`native-logs.err`. tasks.notes: AUTHORING 2026-11-11, estimate 2 h provisional. `model-cache inspect` needs saved manifest, and shared BeeGFS pool has none, so declared-vs-present gate cannot run on it. `model-cache resolve`/`import` once per body (the load-bearing ones first), then `inspect`; gate would caught half-snapshot class without symlink walk — withdrawn `LibertAIDAI` 'stub' reading and ds4 double-count artifact both came from summing/walking tree cache itself could describe. tasks.title: Executor must treat a placement refusal as terminal: no watchdog, no sampler, no retry
tasks.notes: AUTHORING 2026-11-11, estimate 2 h provisional. Measured in the arm-5 verify-route window (`head:~/benchmarks/arm5-verify-route-20261111/boot2-fi073e/`): `sparkrun run` answered `Error: cluster has insufficient free capacity for 4 node(s): Cluster cannot satisfy 4 ranks: only placed 0 of 4 ranks across 4 host(s)` with `GPU has an existing allocation; exclusive ownership prevents sharing [occupied]` on all four hosts — the foreign allocation was the Kimi six-node boot `270298e57de6b5bb_7b621ddf2963` (`sparkrun_270298e57de6b5bb_7b621ddf2963_node_0..5` on `.30`-`.35`) — and the driver continued: it armed a watchdog and a mem-guard anyway, polled against the foreign `sparkrun_*_node_0` container (the poll matched the first container on the node), recorded `verdict=loading ranks=3` against another workstream's serve, and only later killed its strays (eight host samplers; the foreign boot itself loaded its weights normally in 383 s, so no harm that time). A placement refusal is terminal. ACCEPTANCE: the executor stops there — no watchdog, no sampler, no retry, no container-name capture — and a test drives a placement-refusing stub through the executor and asserts no child process launches and the non-zero rc is propagated. CLOSED 2026-11-11 in the executor (`tools/run-arm.sh`): the appearance loop now snapshots the node's container ids before the launch (`PRE_CONTAINERS`/`PRE_IDS`) and accepts only an id that was not there, so it can no longer bind to a peer's `_solo|_node_0`; and a launcher exit whose log carries `insufficient free capacity` / `only placed N of M ranks` / `GPU has an existing allocation` is a terminal placement refusal — it writes `placement-refusal.txt` with the tail, arms no watchdog, no sampler and no guard, retries nothing (the `Execution resources are busy` retry loop runs only before this point), and exits 6 instead of the generic 5. Tests drive the real slice with stub `sparkrun`/`ssh`/`docker`: refusal → rc 6, refusal file, no instrument files; launch → the new container matched and the pre-existing one ignored; plus the ordering guard that the refusal exit precedes `boot-watchdog.py` and `guard-arm`. `bash -n` + `bash-ism-lint` clean, stubs are POSIX `#!/bin/sh`.

tasks.title: Kimi K3.1 indexer needs 64-token kernel blocks; KDA/mamba forces a 5,760-token block and BLHNC
tasks.notes: AUTHORING 2026-11-11, estimate 4 h provisional. Engine-side blocker, not a memory one: the DeepSeek-V32 indexer needs 64-token kernel blocks, while the KDA/mamba alignment forces the KV manager block to 5,760 tokens (`interface.py:1115`, 'Setting attention block size to 5760 tokens'), `--block-size 64` is accepted then overridden, and `utils.py:420` picks the packed BLHNC layout — the layer-compact LBNHC alternative is refused even though `envs.py` lists it, because the resolver requires the explicit layout in every worker's supported set. Measured in boots 5-6 on the six-node TP=2 x PP=3 shape. RESEARCHED 2026-11-11 (`.scratch/kimi-six-engine-verdict-20261111.md`): the pinned image `ghcr.io/spark-arena/dgx-vllm-eugr-nightly@sha256:98a2535b…` runs vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev1016+g06129ab02` (built 2026-11-07) and predates the fix; the upstream fix exists and is merged, vllm-project/vllm#66037, merge commit `4088c283`, 2026-11-09T04:31Z — packed hybrid block size, slot-mapping methods, and honouring `writes_kv_cache_from_block_table()` so packed token caches split into 64-token kernel blocks instead of raising. Not in any release (latest v0.33.0rc3, 2026-11-02), and no published eugr/GB10 nightly is newer than 2026-11-07 (GHCR tags end at `2026110702`, both resolving to the pinned digest; Docker Hub `eugr/spark-vllm` latest 2026-11-07), so the arm waits on a nightly rebuilt from main ≥ `4088c283`. Knob audit ruled out: `--block-size` only raises (the clamp overrides it); LBNHC/LBHNC/BLNHC/BHLNC all refused (supported `['BLHNC']`); `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, kv/mamba dtypes, `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT`, `--mamba-block-size` and a page-size flag do not exist or do not break the clamp. The only public image carrying the fix is `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:c68112d8…` (2026-11-11, main `f5d93296`), a different build line with no eugr SM121 patches — a probe, not the arm's route. ACCEPTANCE: the arm boots on an image built from vLLM main ≥ `4088c283` (#66037); the next-session preflight is `docker run --rm --network none --entrypoint grep <image> -rn map_to_kernel_slot_mapping …/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`, then the boot command in the note (recipe unchanged, image override only, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.82` and the boot4/5 vision cap). #66037 was validated only at TP8 on 2×B300 with dummy weights, so the first GB10/PP3 boot is still an experiment. GUARDRAIL SEMANTICS worth keeping: in boots 2-3 the 6 GiB guard fired AFTER the engine had already freed memory, so the guard was not the cause there — the watchdog's `serve_pid=gone` timestamp is the death evidence, not the guard's trip.

tasks.title: A four-rank boot serves with no lease in either ledger and no window lock
tasks.notes:
Measured 2026-11-11 19:15:59Z-19:31Z, read-only: task `b020d2dd178343a5_55dafcf24cde` runs one rank each on `.31`-`.34` (image `littlecedar/dgx-spark-dsv41:canary-roce-aff52fa5`, id `3f4480818acb`, `Up` and healthy, `/v1/models` 200 serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`) while `.local/fleet-leases.json` is `{"leases":[],"version":1}` (33 B, sha `57247219`, same bytes and mtime on the head copy), `director lease --list` reports 0 live leases, and no `.local/fleet-window.lock` exists. It is not the campaign arm: `state.json` has no `leases` key and reads 10 measured / 13 blocked of 23 with mtime `01:38:06 ET`, and the head clone at `0a6e4b6` carries the lease code (`aa54000`, `ebf5c8e`, `298098d`, `08ff156`). So the claim path the register names as the only one for a multi-machine boot has no record of a live quartet. Acceptance: identify the launching session from its own evidence (argv, receipt dir, sparkrun task owner), then either make that path write a lease or refuse the boot, and show one boot that records and releases it. Not bootable: this row is the audit, not an arm.

CORRECTED 2026-11-11 21:24 ET, after the boot history and the image pin were read: the boot this row measured is **the shipped production arm**, not an unattributed research quartet. `ghcr.io/littlecedar/dgx-spark-dsv41@sha256:7c3cb394…` (`recipes/ds4/deepseek-v4.1-flash-knapcio-tp4-1m-sglang.yaml:20`) resolves on `.31` to image id `3f4480818acb`, tagged `canary-roce-aff52fa5`; its `model_revision: 08c8657f…` is the snapshot in the engine's argv, and TP 4, `max_model_len` 1048576 and DSPARK k=5 all match. Arm 5 is refuted twice: it pins `dsv41-sm121-dg:0.2.1-fi073e` (`sha256:85c1ffc3…`) and sets `SWA_BOUNDED_REPLAY=0`, which the launcher turns into `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`, while the live argv carries the positive flag. The task the 14:38 board named (`…55dafcf24cde`) is gone: the fleet was powered off at 18:31:42 and 19:40:11 ET, then rebooted at 20:02:36 after `apt -y full-upgrade`, and the production serve was relaunched at `2026-11-12T01:34:30Z` as `b020d2dd178343a5_0abd7d020db4`, still with 0 live leases and no window lock. What stays open is the policy question the row was really asking — whether a protected production boot is meant to carry a lease record under the 2026-11-11 S9 answer ('a campaign lease is the only claim for any multi-machine boot') — not an unexplained research boot; production is excluded from research accounting, so it cannot be added to the census. Also noted: the production serve's return satisfies the unblock condition its own notes state for `kimi-superexpert-ref-probe`, `ripple-65b-nvfp4-tp1`, `ripple-65b-nvfp4-dflash2-tp1` and `ripple-65b-bf16-tp2`; lifting them is the director's call, not this row's.
